title: Confounded Means Quarantined: turn an honest loss into a safer Scion

ciFast.note: The release will not be called complete until the exact main commit passes remote formatting, lint, release history, closed-loop tests, proof smoke, main evaluation, build, and bundle budgets.

ciDeep.note: The release changes deterministic evaluation, compiler, and workbook contracts. Its focused 55-test battery and keyless cross-revision receipt audit run locally and in the normal unit suite; no model call, weight training, or external device capture is required.

deploy.note: GitHub Pages deployment and a cache-bypassed production probe remain required after Fast verification passes on the merged release commit.

liveProvider.note: No provider request was needed. The release analyzes two already sealed judge passes and replays deterministic compiler behavior over their exact captured artifacts.

manualHuman.note: This release is explicitly single-model-judge cross-revision analysis. It creates no human, instructor, classroom, independent-review, or multi-judge evidence.

claims.summary: The exact 128-case B/A workbook completed in eight hash-bound chunks and was sealed without a combined plaintext review, while its separately held key remains outside Git.
Dual-order ingestion preserves analysis but approves zero training rows when judge revision/runtime identity differs, and it does not misattribute cross-revision disagreements to position order.

The analysis-only record contains 113/128 agreements and 105 score-qualified stable winners, all for GPT-5.4-mini over the captured Scion-base pipeline in four research domains, without relabeling the result as an adapter or held-out promotion comparison.

Explicit affirmative explanation cues realign 16 of 27 judge-identified local answer-key defects, two placeholder option sets fail admission, and eleven uncertain keys remain unrepaired rather than being semantically guessed.
proofCommands: npx vitest run tests/scion-answer-key-alignment.test.js tests/scion-preference-gate.test.js tests/scion-mc-contract-recovery.test.js

claims.summary: Future reverse-order workbooks can bind verified public model, revision, runtime, and prompt metadata from the first sealed pass before scoring and refuse changed identity or session reuse at completion; no model weight or production adapter changes.
